episodes.189301: Convection formed along the leading edge of a surface front across SE GA in the late afternoon as an upper-level trough passed overhead. Unseasonably cold temperatures in the mid-levels combined with MLCAPE under enough westerly shear produced a few stronger storms that produced sub-severe hail and gusty winds.
episodes.189302: Convection formed along the leading edge of a surface front across SE GA in the late afternoon as an upper-level trough passed overhead. Unseasonably cold temperatures in the mid-levels combined with MLCAPE under enough westerly shear produced a few stronger storms that produced sub-severe hail and gusty winds. Strong storms pressed offshore of the NE FL in the late afternoon with gusty winds.
episodes.189699: A winter storm brought moderate to heavy mountain snow, thunderstorms, rain and gusty winds from March 22nd through March 24th. A brief funnel cloud was observed in Solano County. Periods of chain controls were observed in the mountains.
episodes.189869: A strengthening low-pressure system moving across the Florida Keys brought widespread heavy rainfall to much of South Florida throughout the day on March 22nd, leading to localized flooding.
episodes.189870: A low-pressure system moving across the Florida Keys brought thunderstorms with gusty winds across the nearshore Atlantic waters on the evening of March 22nd and the morning of March 23rd.
episodes.189881: Deep low pressure moving into the West Coast brought a brief period of high wind to portions of southern Nevada. One thunderstorm also brought severe winds to a small portion of the southern Great Basin.
episodes.190429: A wake low on the back side of a strong thunderstorm complex produced very strong wind gusts along the coast. A 59mph wind gust was reported at the Treasure Coast International Airport in Fort Pierce, prompting a High Wind Warning.
episodes.190469: Two distinct rounds of deep, convective organization passed through the Florida Keys as a large upper-level low pressure system slowly evolved over the northern Gulf of Mexico.  Scattered to numerous gale-force wind gusts were recorded by coastal weather instrumentation due to thunderstorm outflow.
episodes.191655: As a upper level low approaches the area, a variety of weather events unfold. Initially an approaching warm air advection brings a warm front and associated precipitation and eventually cold air as the low descends towards our CWA.
